paper.title: Sensor Scheduling in Intrusion Detection Games with Uncertain Payoffs

settings.name_in_paper: Intrusion detection zero-sum game, known payoff (NE computation via Distributed Weighted Majority)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Computing approximate Nash equilibria of a known zero-sum matrix game (learning in games with equilibrium objective).
unmapped: Defender's strategy set is product of |S| sensors each with |Theta| orientations (|Theta|^|S| joint strategies); payoff is additive across sensors
Payoff matrix fully known; intruder best-responds via LP
Objective is an epsilon-Nash equilibrium (game-value approximation)
settings.definition_quote: We model this as a 2-player zero-sum game over a graph, where the defender (Player 1) seeks to identify the optimal strategy for scheduling sensor orientations to minimize the probability of missed detection at minimal cost

settings.name_in_paper: Intrusion detection game with unknown homogeneous sensor models (bandit feedback)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in a zero-sum matrix game; regret is measured relative to the game value (equilibrium objective).
unmapped: Payoff matrix A_ij = V_ij log(1-p_detect) + c_i - r_j parametrized by a single unknown Bernoulli detection probability
Learner knows costs c_i, r_j, coverage counts V_ij and the interval [p_min, p_max] containing p_detect
Defender observes intruder's pure strategy j_t and V_{i_t j_t} Bernoulli detection samples
Regret defined as sum_t (x_t^T A y_t - V*_A), relative to game value
Opponent plays mixed strategies y_t (either a NE of the true game or arbitrary)
settings.definition_quote: We will first consider the setting with homogenous sensors, where the game matrix $A$ can be parametrized by a single (unknown) Bernoulli distribution with parameter $p_{detect}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Intrusion detection game with unknown heterogeneous sensor models (bandit feedback)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Learning in a zero-sum matrix game; regret is measured relative to the game value (equilibrium objective).
unmapped: Payoff A_ij = sum_l V_ij,l log(1-p_detect,l) + c_i - r_j with one unknown Bernoulli parameter per sensor
Learner knows costs, coverage counts and per-sensor intervals [p_min,l, p_max,l]
Defender observes intruder's pure strategy and per-sensor detection samples
Regret defined relative to the game value V*_A
settings.definition_quote: We will now consider the setting with heterogeneous sensors, i.e., each sensor has a different probability of detection. In this setting, the game's payoff matrix $A$ can be parameterized by a set of $|\mathcal{S}|$ Bernoulli distributions

algorithms.name: Online Learning and Adaptation of Strategies for Homogenous Sensors (Algorithm 2)
Online Learning and Adaptation of Strategies for Heterogeneous Sensors (adapted UCB for matrix games, Algorithm 3)

symbols.L_tilde: upper bound on min_i sum_t sum_q loss of the defender over T iterations (can be bounded by T)

source.label: thm:dwm
source.quote: Let $\{ x_1, \hdots, x_T \}$ and $\{ y_1, \hdots, y_T \}$ be the mixed strategies returned by Algorithm 1 after $T$ iterations with $\beta = (1+ \sqrt{2 |\mathcal{S}|ln|\Theta|/\Tilde{L}})^{-1}$ ... The pair $(\Bar{x},\Bar{y})$ approximates the game's Nash Equilibrium value within $\epsilon_T$

results.notes: Bound on approximation of the NE value by averaged strategies (deterministic); not a regret. Follows from Freund & Schapire 1996. Probability field set to expectation for lack of a deterministic option.

bound.regime: y_t = y^dagger (intruder plays a NE of the true game)

symbols.V_max: max_{i,j} V_ij, maximum number of covered nodes on a path
symbols.p_max: upper bound on the detection probability

conditions: Assumption 1: p_detect in [p_min, p_max] with 0<p_min<p_max<1, independent detections
intruder plays a Nash equilibrium y^dagger of the true game

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Under Assumption 1, for a specified $\alpha \in (0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\alpha$, Algorithm 2 has the following guarantees ... $\mathcal{R}_T \leq \frac{5 \sqrt{2} V_{max}}{(1-p_{max})} \sqrt{T \log{\frac{2T}{\alpha}}}; y_t = y^{\dagger}$

results.notes: Paper's alpha is the failure probability delta. Regret is relative to game value V*_A. Algorithm does not use T, so marked anytime (bound itself depends on T via union bound).

bound.regime: y_t != y^dagger (intruder does not play a NE)

symbols.p_max: upper bound on the detection probability

conditions: Assumption 1: p_detect in [p_min, p_max] with 0<p_min<p_max<1, independent detections
intruder's y_t is not a NE of the true game

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: $\mathcal{R}_T \leq \frac{2 \sqrt{2} V_{max}}{(1-p_{max})} \sqrt{T \log{\frac{2T}{\alpha}}}; y_t \neq y^{\dagger}$ (i.e., $y_t$ is not a NE of $\mathcal{G}$), where $V_{max} = \max_{i,j} V_{ij}$ and $p_{max}$ is the maximum probability of detection of the sensors.

results.notes: Paper's alpha = delta. Regret relative to game value V*_A.

source.label: thm:ucb_regret
source.quote: Let Assumption 1 hold and let $T \ge |\mathcal{S}||\Theta||J|\ge 2$, $\delta = 1/(2T^2|\mathcal{S}||\Theta||J|)$, $C = \bar{V}_{max}/(1-\bar{p}_{max})$. When Algorithm 1 in \cite{o2021matrix} is applied ... the regret is bounded as: $\mathcal{R}_T \leq 1 + C |\mathcal{S}|\sqrt{2 |\Theta||J|T \log(4T^2|\mathcal{S}||\Theta||J|)}$

results.notes: Holds with probability at least 1-delta (per proof). Regret relative to game value.

cited_results.setting_description: Zero-sum matrix games with bandit feedback (1-sub-Gaussian noisy payoffs), regret vs game value, |I| x |J| matrix
